title: API Gateway Pricing Explained: Costs and Tips (2026)
summary: API Gateway pricing charges per request and data transfer, with no monthly fee and a free first year. Estimate what you'll pay based on your traffic.
body_markdown:
## Unexpected charges and hard limits


**Nothing in the per-million-request rate covers the surprises** : the always-on cache, data transfer out, log storage and a few hard limits. Each needs its own line in your estimate.


### The case that the request rate is the whole bill


If you never enable a cache, never log bodies and serve small responses, the add-ons barely register, and the request rate is the bill. That is the strongest counter-argument, and it holds for low-volume, uncached APIs.


Once a requirement, such as latency, an audit trail or an inspection layer, switches on a feature billed by the hour or by the gigabyte, the claim stops holding.


### Data transfer, caching and logging


**A provisioned REST cache bills every hour it exists, traffic or not.** Per C3x, the smallest, 0.5 GB, costs $0.02 an hour, or[$14.60 a month](https://kejyuntw.gitbooks.io/aws-learning-notes/content/api-gateway/api-gateway-pricing.html) , which is easy to absorb.


At 1.6 GB it's $0.038 an hour and $27.74 a month, which means about $330 per year.


At 6.1 GB the price jumps to $0.20 an hour and $146 a month, ten times the entry size. That means a cache sized "to be safe" can cost more than the requests it saves.


Beyond that point, sizes climb steadily. 13.5 GB is $0.25 an hour ($182.50 a month), 28.4 GB is $0.50 ($365), and 58.2 GB is $1.00 ($730).


The top size, 237 GB, reaches about $2,774 a month, so a cache sized for a worst case becomes a standing cost larger than many whole services.


*The chart shows monthly cost climbing from $14.60 at 0.5 GB to about $2,774 at 237 GB in us-east-1, so your data volume will determine whether you spend $15 or $2,774 monthly.


The lesson is that cost scales with the memory you reserve, not the hits you get.*


Size the cache to your hot set of responses, then check the hit rate before stepping up a tier.


### Data transfer out and logs


Anything leaving AWS is billed as data transfer out per gigabyte, and CloudWatch access logs are billed for ingestion and storage. Logs deserve a second look because they can hold request data, which carries retention and location obligations of its own.


### API Gateway payload size and timeout limits


Because REST APIs cap payloads at 10 MB and default to a 29-second integration timeout, large uploads and slow backends need a different pattern, such as direct-to-storage uploads or asynchronous jobs.


Finding that out after launch means rebuilding the request path, so check both limits against your heaviest call before choosing an API type.


Where the asynchronous job is only a Lambda function that receives a webhook and calls SaaS tools, Activepieces can take that work instead, and its[pricing page](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) , checked 21 November 2026, lists a run as 1 credit however many steps it has.


A three-step webhook handler and a ten-step one meter identically, where Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's per module, and the free plan includes 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows.
